clue.text: Whitewash edges of door, lid off container

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its two outermost letters, so only the first and last are kept
taking the lid off something removes its top, which in a word is the opening letter

blocks.note: the first and last letters of door
a tub is a container

explanation.surface: A decorator paints round a door, having levered the lid off a paint tin.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitewash is a decorating word here, but the definition is its sporting sense; TUB loses its T to leave UB.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a whitewash is a crushing defeat with no reply, and to drub is to beat an opponent thoroughly.

clue.text: Finally, convict put out in cell block?

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word that follows it

blocks.note: the last letter of convict
to put out a statement or publication is to issue it

explanation.surface: A prisoner is finally ejected into the cell block of a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The prison picture makes 'cell block' sound like a wing of a jail; the question mark flags that the cells are biological.
explanation.definitionFit: Biological tissue is a mass of similar cells grouped together, so a block of cells, playfully.

clue.text: Still without a proposal?

blocks.note: a motion is a formal proposal put to a meeting
less can mean without, as in 'a year less a day'

explanation.surface: Is a meeting still stuck with nothing put forward for debate?
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads in reverse order: the proposal comes first in the answer, followed by the word for without.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still is not moving at all, which is exactly what being without movement means.

clue.text: Rival of Athens, region in South Africa

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the abbreviation that follows it

blocks.note: SA is the standard abbreviation for South Africa
a part of a country is a region of it

explanation.surface: Some ancient Greek city appears to have a counterpart region in modern South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek city-state that fought Athens in the Peloponnesian War was its great military rival.

clue.text: South opposed to past capital

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for south
anti means against or opposed
ago means in the past, as in 'long ago'

explanation.surface: The South was opposed to the old capital, as in some historic regional quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Past capital' sounds like a former capital, but the definition is just the final word.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital city of Chile, so it is a capital in the sense of seat of government.

clue.text: Light entertainment provided here

blocks.note: first meaning: pale in colour, as of hair or skin
second meaning: a funfair, a place of rides and amusements

explanation.surface: Light entertainment, the comedy and variety kind on television, is on offer at this venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light entertainment' reads as one TV genre; the split falls after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair hair is pale-coloured, and a fair is a travelling show of rides, stalls and amusements.

clue.text: Awkward son taught

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees
to be trained is to have been taught

explanation.surface: A gawky boy is being given lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A strained conversation or atmosphere is forced and uncomfortable, which is what awkward means here.

clue.text: Gracious, angelic quality of yours truly?

blocks.note: first meaning: an exclamation of surprise, as in 'Good gracious!'
second meaning, read literally: the virtue belonging to me, since yours truly is the speaker

explanation.surface: A boastful speaker praises their own kindly, saintly nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gracious' looks like an adjective for the angelic speaker, but it is the exclamation; yours truly is a jokey way of saying I or me.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild oath of surprise like 'gracious me', and literally names the virtue that belongs to me.

clue.text: Horn, I gathered – on this animal?

definitions.text: Horn, I gathered – on this animal?

indicators.note: things gathered together are bunched up anyhow, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone surmises that a horn grows on a particular beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gathered' reads as 'I understood'; the whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is the animal famous for the horn on its nose, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Uncivilised lot, parents, a strangely unknown quantity

indicators.note: something arranged strangely is out of its normal order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Parents complain that their unruly children are a strangely unknown quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: The peasantry, as a social class, was traditionally sneered at by snobs as rough and unrefined.

clue.text: Top deck on public transport?

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another is placed after it, so the deck comes second

blocks.note: a bus is a form of public transport
a deck is a level or tier, as on a double-decker

explanation.surface: It sounds like the upper deck of a double-decker bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top deck' reads as one phrase, but Top is the definition: a garment, not the upstairs of the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustier is a close-fitting strapless garment worn on the upper body, so a kind of top.

clue.text: Terrible current cost to bear when China defeated and fiasco ends

indicators.note: ends asks for the final letter of each of the words before it

blocks.clueFragment: cost to bear when China defeated
blocks.note: the last letter of each of these six words
the last letter of fiasco

explanation.surface: A long-winded report on the price paid after a Chinese defeat and a final disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is deliberately rambling; 'and' only joins, and is not one of the words whose final letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirling column of air, a destructive current of wind.

clue.text: Common political activist

blocks.note: first meaning: a village ..., an area of common land
second meaning: a member or campaigner of an environmentalist party

explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' looks like an adjective describing the activist, but it is the noun for shared village land.
explanation.definitionFit: Common land in a village is a grassy open space, and an environmental campaigner belongs to the Green movement.

clue.text: Amazed lip bleeding after this, perhaps?

blocks.note: first meaning: utterly astonished, a British slang word
second meaning, read literally: having been punched in the mouth, gob being slang for mouth

explanation.surface: Someone is stunned to find their lip bleeding after an incident.
explanation.walkthrough: Gob is British slang for mouth, so the slang word for astonished also describes a mouth that has been hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang term means flabbergasted, as if struck in the face; taken literally it is a punch in the mouth.

clue.text: Sailor with one day left

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a common crossword sailor
and means together with
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A seaman is given a single day remaining of shore leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like 'remaining', but the definition is its other sense: deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left behind and deserted has been abandoned by its owner.

clue.text: Up-and-down opener in no-win situation, some fiddle

blocks.note: a draw is a result where nobody wins
the bridge is part of a fiddle, holding the strings up

explanation.surface: A musician caught in a stalemate fiddles with a lid that goes up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some fiddle' suggests a cheat or a hidden word, but it means a part of the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle drawbridge is raised and lowered to open or close the entrance, so it opens by going up and down.

clue.text: Location of what divides us, not going any further

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: whatever separates two people sits in the gap linking the pair
second meaning: the phrase said to mark a confidence that must stay secret

explanation.surface: Two people discuss the gulf separating them and agree it will stop there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not going any further' sounds like the end of a journey; it is the promise that a secret stays private.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase prefaces a confidential remark, and literally names the space separating two people.

clue.text: Element in cask gets mixed with nitrogen

indicators.note: mixed up means stirred together, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: a tun is a large cask for beer or wine
taken as written
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A chemical element inside a barrel is blended with nitrogen gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten is a metallic chemical element, symbol W, used in light bulb filaments.

clue.text: Western Asian states formerly in decline are as tempting

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling these four words

explanation.surface: A report on Asian countries whose past downturns now make them attractive investments.
explanation.definitionFit: Near East is the older name for the countries of south-west Asia, now usually called the Middle East.

clue.text: Vertical hole he-man ruptured with fist

indicators.note: something ruptured is burst apart, so the letters are broken and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muscleman punches straight through a wall, leaving a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineshaft is a deep, upright passage sunk into the ground to reach a mine.

clue.text: Chinese thinking Maoist converted

indicators.note: something converted has been changed into a new form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A follower of Mao has been won over to traditional Chinese philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Taoism is the ancient Chinese philosophy and religion founded on the teachings of Laozi.

clue.text: Head of bank with responsibility for extra money

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of bank
an onus is a responsibility or duty

explanation.surface: A bank's boss, accountable for the business, collects an extra payout.
explanation.walkthrough: The bank chief's payout is in the picture, which makes the definition easy to overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an additional payment on top of normal wages, such as a banker's annual reward.

clue.text: One idiot or another from Belfast?

blocks.note: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
a twit is another word for an idiot

explanation.surface: Calling someone a fool, or perhaps a different fool from Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The other idiot comes from Belfast, so the Northern Ireland abbreviation goes in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a foolish, silly person, a synonym for an idiot.

clue.text: Rush to trap rat in container

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a case is a container
a rat and a cad are both treacherous, dishonourable men

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to catch a rodent in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: The rat is a scoundrel, not a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a rushing fall of water, and to cascade is to pour down rapidly.

clue.text: Top copy that's wrong

blocks.note: to ape is to copy or imitate
a cross marks an answer wrong

explanation.surface: The top copy of a document turns out to be incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top copy' reads as one phrase, an office term for an original document; Top is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or summit of something, such as a triangle or a mountain.

clue.text: In lexicographical reference, 'hand' forgotten

indicators.note: In says one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: The word hand has been left out of a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something omitted has been left out or overlooked, much as something forgotten has been.

clue.text: A bit lower

blocks.note: first meaning: a small amount of liquid
second meaning: to let something down or reduce it

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'slightly lower'; the split falls between 'A bit' and 'lower'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop is a tiny quantity, and to drop something is to let it fall or bring it down.

clue.text: Break last of massive optical devices covering half of vent

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the following word
half of keeps only the front half of the word that follows
covering means wrapping around, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the last letter of massive
lenses are optical devices
the first half of vent

explanation.surface: Enormous telescopes partly block an air vent.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning break for tea or coffee and a snack, taken around eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pause from work in the late morning is a break, the snack time known by this name.

clue.text: Stringed instrument? No thanks: old Latin American instrument

indicators.note: No here means without, so the word after it is taken away

blocks.note: a guitar is a stringed instrument
ta is British slang for thanks
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone declines the offer of a guitar in favour of a vintage Latin American instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No thanks' reads as a polite refusal; it means remove the word for thanks from the guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: The guiro is a notched gourd scraped with a stick, a percussion instrument from Latin America.
